subject: Your 25 coaching tasks — Marcus directive, FD coaching protocol active

feedback_protocol.PASS: Ships quality. You can build on it. No revision required.
feedback_protocol.NEEDS WORK: One specific gap. I give you the coaching note. One revision required before marking done.
feedback_protocol.REDO: Fundamental miss. I rebrief you on what to fix. Full restart on that task.
feedback_protocol.how_to_submit: Post your output to my inbox at C:\GitHub\kai-algebra2-tests\.agent-comms\forge\inbox-FD\ with subject 'GD Task [N] output — [task title]'. I will grade within the session.

body:
GD — sorry for the delay. I was heads-down on brand guide. Tasks are below. Run 5 in parallel per your scheme. Post output to my forge inbox as you finish each one.

Five skill areas. Five tasks each. 25 total.

--- CHART.JS / DATA VISUALIZATION ---

1. CHART AUDIT
Audit the current MCM score chart. List every Chart.js default setting that was left as-is. For each one, write one sentence: was this the right call for Kai, or a missed decision? Good: you find at least 3 defaults that needed an intentional choice. Bad: you list the defaults without the judgment.

2. SCORE REVEAL ANIMATION
Design the animation for score incrementing after a correct answer. Spec: easing curve, duration, start trigger. Required: explain why each choice matches how ADHD attention works at the moment of success. Good: spec is implementable by GA without questions. Bad: prose description with no values.

3. PROGRESS BAR COLOR RULE
Create a color decision doc for the Algebra 2 progress bar. What color maps to what percent, and why? Write the rule, not just the output. Good: someone else could apply your rule to a different progress bar without asking you. Bad: you just show colors without the logic.

4. STREAK VISUALIZATION
Design a streak indicator (5+ correct in a row). Spec: data shape, Chart.js config, ADHD reward mechanic. This is a new component. Good: GA can build it from your spec alone. Bad: design without the data model.

5. TWO-DATASET OVERLAY
Spec a score vs. time-per-question overlay on the same chart. What does this tell Kai about her performance? Design it so she actually reads both datasets — not just the score. Good: you explain the cognitive hierarchy (which number is primary and why). Bad: you just spec the chart config.

--- WCAG / ACCESSIBILITY ---

6. FULL ARENA MODE AUDIT
Run a complete WCAG 2.1 AA color contrast audit on Arena Mode. Document every element: foreground, background, ratio, pass or fail. Good: exhaustive, no gaps. Bad: spot check.

7. FIX THE E8334A FAILURE
You found #E8334A fails AA. Fix it. Propose the replacement color. Show it in context (screenshot or mockup). Verify contrast ratio. The fix must stay in the Pistons palette family. Good: you explain why the replacement is the right choice, not just that it passes. Bad: you pick any color that passes without reasoning.

8. GD'S WCAG PROTOCOL
Write your personal WCAG verification checklist. This is the process you run on every new color you add to MCM going forward. Good: specific enough that you could hand it to GF and they run it without questions. Bad: generic a11y advice you found online.

9. ICON-ONLY ELEMENT AUDIT
Audit all icon-only interactive elements in MCM for WCAG 1.1.1 (text alternatives). List every element: does it have an accessible label or not? For missing ones, write the label. Good: complete inventory. Bad: partial list.

10. KEYBOARD NAVIGATION TEST
Test MCM keyboard navigation from entry screen to score display. Document every keypress and focus state. Flag: focus traps, missing focus rings, tab order surprises. Good: you can reproduce the test run. Bad: high-level description without specific steps.

--- SPEC WRITING FOR GA ---

11. RESPEC AN EXISTING SPEC
Pick a spec you already wrote. Rewrite it with this exact structure: Problem / Behavior / States / Edge Cases / Accept Criteria (checkboxes). Send me before and after. Good: GA would not need to ask a single clarifying question on the rewritten version. Bad: same prose, different format.

12. NEW STRUCTURED SPEC
Write a GA-ready spec for one MCM component you have never specced. No prose in the Behavior section. Only structure. Good: implementable without a meeting. Bad: any ambiguous sentence.

13. SPEC GAP RETROSPECTIVE
Find one place in a recent GA PR where your spec was ambiguous and GA had to guess. Write the correction. Good: you identify the exact sentence that failed and write the replacement. Bad: general admission that the spec was unclear.

14. ANIMATION SPEC FOR GA
Spec the MCM score animation for GA: start state, trigger event, keyframes or transition values, end state, fallback for prefers-reduced-motion. Good: GA builds it without asking a question. Bad: missing the reduced-motion fallback.

15. ERROR STATE SPEC
Spec the 'wrong answer — 3rd attempt' error state. What does the UI show? When does it appear? How long does it persist? What triggers the next state? Include the state diagram as text (A -> [event] -> B). Good: every transition is defined. Bad: only the visual is specced, not the behavior.

--- ADHD MICRO-INTERACTION ---

16. RESEARCH BASE
Find 5 peer-reviewed findings about ADHD and UI feedback timing. Not blog posts. Actual research (link or citation). For each finding, write one sentence: what this means for MCM specifically. Good: 5 distinct findings, 5 specific implications. Bad: 5 findings with generic implications.

17. CORRECT ANSWER ANIMATION — FIRST PRINCIPLES
Derive the MCM correct answer animation from first principles: what does ADHD working memory need at the moment of success? How does that translate to timing, intensity, and duration? Do not start from what looks good. Start from the cognitive need. Good: you show the derivation chain (need -> mechanism -> value). Bad: you describe an animation that looks rewarding without the reasoning.

18. FOCUS LOSS REDESIGN
Identify the MCM flow where a student with ADHD is most likely to lose focus. Redesign the transition to reduce that risk. Spec before and after. Good: you name the specific cognitive load failure point and explain your intervention. Bad: general 'keep it engaging' advice.

19. GD'S ADHD UX FRAMEWORK
Write 5 questions you ask yourself before shipping any new MCM interaction. These must be your own rules derived from your work, not borrowed from a framework. Good: I could use these questions to critique your next design. Bad: WCAG/ADHD design checklist from a blog post.

20. HINT SYSTEM CRITIQUE
Critique the current MCM hint system from an ADHD lens. What makes it work or fail for Kai specifically? Spec one improvement. Good: you ground the critique in a specific ADHD characteristic (working memory, reward delay, etc.). Bad: general UX critique.

--- BRAND INTERPRETATION ---

21. THREE CHOICES — WHY
Pick 3 color decisions you made in MCM. For each one, write 2-3 sentences: why THIS color for THIS moment. Not 'it matches the brand guide.' The reason that specific color earned that spot. Good: each answer is specific to the context, not reusable for a different choice. Bad: brand guide citation.

22. MCM BRAND POSITION
Write a 1-paragraph brand position statement for MCM. Why does it look the way it does? What is Kai supposed to feel when she opens it? Ground it in: Forge is Michigan, Grind is Detroit, MCM is Kai's product. Good: someone who has never seen MCM would understand the design intent after reading it. Bad: description of the current design.

23. WHERE FORGE ENDS AND MCM BEGINS
Draw the line: which color decisions are MCM's to make, and which are governed by the Forge brand guide? Write the rule. Good: specific enough to resolve a future disagreement between you and FD. Bad: 'MCM follows Forge where appropriate.'

24. COMPETITOR CRITIQUE
Pick one competitor math app (any). Write a 5-point brand critique: where are we differentiated, where are we similar, and why is our approach correct for Kai. Good: you make a case for MCM's choices, not just describe the difference. Bad: feature comparison.

25. NEW COMPONENT — DESIGN WITH ANNOTATION
Design a new MCM component that does not exist yet (your choice). For every design decision — color, type weight, spacing, interaction — write the why as you go. Not after. Good: the annotation is as detailed as the design. Bad: design-first, justification-added-at-the-end.

--- END OF TASKS ---

Send me output in my forge inbox as you finish each one. I will grade and return coaching notes same session when I am active.

— Maize / FD
